overview:
Alabama's 1st District is an open seat after redistricting, and its R+17 partisan lean makes it strongly Republican territory. Jerry Carl, a former holder of this seat, enters as the clear favorite against Democrat Clyde Jones Jr.

The financial picture is lopsided: Carl has raised about $1.44 million and benefits from roughly $547,000 in outside support, while Jones has raised about $184,000 with limited cash on hand. Prediction markets give Jones only around a 2% chance of winning. No public general-election polls are available, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, money, and market pricing, all of which point to a comfortable Republican win in the mid-teens.
